holding_summary: A tenant operating a boarding/rooming house recovering nuisance damages may elect to be compensated for the loss in usable value of the premises, including rent reductions given to retain boarders, rather than for depreciation in overall rental value. The verdict was reversed only because evidence of outside laundry costs was admitted without proof the price paid was reasonable.

quotes.text: She was using the premises as a rooming and boarding house.

She was, therefore, entitled to recover the loss sustained by being deprived of the use of the rear of the premises and the loss she sustained by being obliged to reduce the rental of her rooms in order to keep her tenants.

notes: Core holding is a nuisance-damages-measure ruling; the court never adjudicates the legality/characterization of the boarding-house letting itself, only recognizes and protects its rental value, so characterization is left null.
Dispute over enforceability of a building-setback restrictive covenant between vacant-lot owners; no mention of lodgers, boarders, or compensated occupancy.

Upholds mandatory replacement of school sinks with water closets in tenement houses as a valid police-power sanitation measure; concerns building plumbing code compliance generally, not compensated room-letting or boarding-house regulation specifically.
Restrictive-covenant/nuisance dispute over construction of an automobile garage; no letting of rooms or dwellings to occupants.

Construes a restrictive covenant against erecting a 'tenement house,' holding modern apartment houses fall outside it; concerns building-type classification for covenant purposes, not compensated occupancy of rooms/lodgers.

Fraudulent-conveyance/constructive-trust case about title to real property purchased with a daughter's savings; passing mention that she 'assisted in serving and waiting upon boarders and lodgers, kept by her mother' is background biographical detail, not a ruling on the letting arrangement.
Landlord-tenant dispute over a lessor's failure to deliver possession of a commercial 'store' floor occupied by a holdover tenant; no lodging or boarding-house facts.
Cotenant accounting for use and occupation of a shop/blacksmith property in partition; no compensated lodging of a dwelling.
Life tenant's right to sue a sub-tenant for waste to timber; no relation to letting rooms/dwellings for pay.
Municipal liability for a collapsed reservoir dam damaging town bridges/highways; unrelated to lodging or room-letting.
Strikes down a horseshoer licensing/examination statute as an invalid exercise of the police power; a police-power precedent generally but not about lodging-house licensing or letting rooms.
Restrictive-covenant dispute over conversion of a private-dwelling-house lot to store use; addresses structural vs. use covenants generally, not compensated lodging/room-letting.

holding_summary: The court held that a written lease complete on its face merges all prior oral negotiations, so parol evidence of the landlord's alleged prior oral promise to complete repairs before the tenant's term began was inadmissible to vary the lease. The judgment for the tenant, who had rented the premises to let out furnished rooms, was accordingly reversed.

quotes.text: all oral negotiations taking place prior to or at the time a written agreement is executed are merged in it

notes: Premises were 'rented for the purpose of letting furnished rooms,' but the opinion gives no further detail on scale (single lodger vs. multiple) or on the tenant's relation to lodgers, and the holding is pure parol-evidence/merger doctrine with no ruling on the legal character of the room-letting itself -- polarity and characterization left null, and who_was_letting/duration left unclear for lack of supporting facts.
Proceeding to appoint a committee for an incompetent person who resided in an apartment hotel; the apartment-hotel residence is incidental biography, not a ruling on letting/lodging.

holding_summary: In an equity nuisance suit by a boarding-house proprietor against a village sewage-disposal plant, the court held the proper measure of damages is the difference between the rental value of the plaintiff's property before and after the nuisance, not separate recovery for physical discomfort or sickness. It also held the statutory requirement to file a claim with the village clerk for negligence injuries did not apply to this equitable nuisance action.

quotes.text: the proprietor of a boarding house

The measure of damages recoverable in such a case is the difference between the rental value of the plaintiff’s property prior to the erection and maintenance of the sewage plant and its value thereafter.

notes: Court protects and monetizes the boarding-house keeper's rental/letting value against a municipal nuisance, but never classifies the legal character of the boarder arrangements themselves, so characterization is left null.
Injunction-pleading dispute between a commercial-loft assignee and the landlord; no lodging or dwelling-letting facts.
Mechanic's-lien dispute over construction of an apartment hotel; 'apartment hotel' is only the building type under construction, with no discussion of letting or occupancy arrangements.

Dispute over ownership of life-insurance proceeds between a widow and the insured's children; a witness is identified as 'a boarding-house keeper' only to date events, with no bearing on the letting question.
